label: FRITZ!Powerline 1220E powerline adapter
description: HomePlug AV2 powerline adapter with two gigabit RJ45 ports and an integrated 230 V socket with line filter, so it does not cost the wall outlet it uses. Up to 1200 Mbit/s on the mains wiring; no radios.
notes: AVM technical specifications: '2 x gigabit LAN (10/100/1000 Base-T, RJ45 port)', 'Up to 1200 Mbit/s powerline data throughput ... according to the powerline standard HomePlug AV2', integrated 230 V socket with line filter, 128-bit AES link encryption, IGMP multicast, 3 LEDs, ~1 W standby / ~3 W operating, 59 x 132 x 41 mm, 220 g. Backwards compatible with 1200/500/200 Mbit/s adapters and IEEE P1901 - which is why a 500M adapter on the same mains segment drags the link down to 500M, a behaviour the simulator models by negotiating the powerline medium down rather than up. Rate note: AVM's 1200 Mbit/s is the HomePlug AV2 PHY rate; the simulator's mains medium ladder for powerline ports is 200/1000/1700/2500 Mbps with no 1200 rung, so this port is declared at 1G - the HomePlug AV2 figure the engine can carry - rather than inventing a rate the cage rejects.
